class.name: ALManager
class.description: Global OpenAL device and mixer control, registered as an [Engine] singleton - reach it from any script as [code]ALManager[/code], at any time, with no scene-tree node required. The output device, sample rate, HRTF, max reverb sends, and max mono/stereo sources used for the one device open at game start come from Project Settings ([code]audio/vaudio/output_device[/code], [code]audio/vaudio/sample_rate[/code], [code]audio/vaudio/hrtf_enabled[/code], [code]audio/vaudio/hrtf[/code], [code]audio/vaudio/max_reverb_sends[/code], [code]audio/vaudio/max_mono_sources[/code], [code]audio/vaudio/max_stereo_sources[/code]), not from this singleton - [method set_output_device], [method set_hrtf] and [method set_hrtf_enabled] are the exceptions, letting a shipped game's audio settings menu change them at runtime. Custom HRTFs: place OpenAL Soft [code].mhr[/code] files in the [code]audio/vaudio/hrtf_folder[/code] folder (default [code]res://hrtf[/code]) and they're listed alongside OpenAL Soft's built-in HRTF, using the file name without its extension. Custom HRTFs are listed before the built-in one, so with the [code]Default[/code] setting OpenAL Soft uses the first custom HRTF. They're bundled into exports automatically. SOFA ([code].sofa[/code]) HRTF datasets can be converted to [code].mhr[/code] with OpenAL Soft's [code]makemhr[/code] utility, e.g. [code]makemhr -i subject.sofa -o subject.mhr[/code].

method.name: get_available_devices
method.description: Returns the names of the playback devices currently available on this machine.

method.name: get_available_capture_devices
method.description: Returns the names of the capture (input/microphone) devices currently available on this machine.

method.name: set_output_device
method.description: Switches the playback device at runtime, reopening the OpenAL device and context and reusing the current sample rate, HRTF, and max reverb sends settings. Every existing AL object (sources, buffers, filters, effects) is invalidated by this. Pass an empty string to use the driver's default device. Returns [code]false[/code] on failure.

method.name: get_available_hrtfs
method.description: Returns the names of the HRTFs OpenAL Soft can use, including any [code].mhr[/code] files in the [code]audio/vaudio/hrtf_folder[/code] folder. Pass one of these to [method set_hrtf].

method.name: set_hrtf
method.description: Switches to the named HRTF at runtime, without interrupting playing sounds. Pass an empty string to use OpenAL Soft's default HRTF. If the name isn't found, the default HRTF is used and a warning is logged. Returns [code]false[/code] if the device couldn't be reset.

method.name: get_hrtf
method.description: Returns the HRTF name last passed to [method set_hrtf] or set in [code]audio/vaudio/hrtf[/code], or an empty string for the default HRTF.

method.name: get_active_hrtf
method.description: Returns the name of the HRTF OpenAL Soft is actually using, or an empty string if HRTF is not active (e.g. it's disabled, or the output isn't stereo).

method.name: set_hrtf_enabled
method.description: Turns HRTF on or off at runtime, without interrupting playing sounds. HRTF is intended for headphones - players using speakers may prefer it off. Returns [code]false[/code] if the device couldn't be reset.

method.name: get_hrtf_enabled
method.description: Returns whether HRTF is requested, from [method set_hrtf_enabled] or [code]audio/vaudio/hrtf_enabled[/code].

method.name: set_master_volume
method.description: Sets the overall output volume, as a linear multiplier. 1.0 is unchanged, 0.0 is silent. Safe to call at any time.

members.member: How volume attenuates with distance from the listener. One of OpenAL's distance model constants (Inverse Distance Clamped, Inverse Distance, Linear Distance Clamped, Linear Distance, Exponent Distance Clamped, Exponent Distance, or None). Safe to change at any time.

How many meters one world unit represents, for OpenAL's own air-absorption and reverb decay calculations. This is separate from [member VAWorld.meters_per_unit], which only affects vaudio's raytracing/acoustics model. Safe to change at any time.

The speed of sound, in meters per second, used for OpenAL's Doppler effect calculation. This is separate from [member VAWorld.speed_of_sound], which only affects vaudio's raytracing/acoustics model. Safe to change at any time.
If [code]true[/code], every sound's direct path is silenced so only reverb is audible. A diagnostic toggle for tuning reverb in isolation.
